title: Beyond the square-root exponent for depth-three circuits
analyst_role: family analyst (paper + Lean, text level; Lean not built); no reasoning trace exists for 112
base_library_L: Mathlib d13f23b + the 12 entries of the inline thebibliography (references.tex): ABI86, DHMTW14, ER60, GKPRT26, GPPST24, H89, HJP95, IPZ01, Krawczyk94, PPSZ05, PPZ99, PSZ00

main_statement.latex:
\label{thm:main}
There is a language \(L\subseteq\bits^*\), a deterministic Turing machine
deciding \(L\), and fixed positive integers \(C,a\) such that the machine
runs in time at most \(C(n+1)^a\) on every input of length \(n\).
If \(f_n\) is the membership function of \(L\) on \(\bits^n\), then
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_2 S_3(f_n)}{\sqrt n}=\infty.
\]
Equivalently, for every real \(A>0\), there is an integer \(N_A\)
such that
\[
 S_3(f_n)>2^{A\sqrt n}\qquad\text{for every }n\ge N_A.
\]
No uniformity or bottom fan-in restriction is imposed on the circuits.
main_statement.paraphrase: There is one language L in deterministic polynomial time whose n-bit membership function needs more than 2^{A sqrt n} gates (all gates counted) in any unbounded fan-in OR-AND-OR circuit, for every constant A > 0 and all large n. The language and machine are fixed before A.

constructive_core.paraphrase: Two structural statements: (1) Lemma restriction lifts correlation bounds from width-b CNFs to width-k CNFs under p-restrictions with constant pk, at expected cost 1/(1-theta) independent of clause count; (2) Prop good-slices gives a slice whose random restrictions have corr_b <= 2^{-|T|/8} with failure probability 4 2^{-m0/16}.

lean_comparator.name: DepthThree
lean_comparator.verbatim: exists (L : List Bool -> Bool) (M : FiniteMultiTapeMachine) (C a : N), 0 < C /\ 0 < a /\ (forall w, MultiTapeHaltsIn M w (L w) (C * (w.length + 1) ^ a)) /\ forall A : R, 0 < A -> exists N, forall n >= N, forall D : Circuit3 (Fin n), D.Computes (fun x => L (List.ofFn x)) -> 2 ^ (A * sqrt n) < D.gateCount

definitions_unfolded.Circuit3: bottom : Fin bottomCount -> RawClause V (list of literals or Boolean constants), middle : Fin middleCount -> Finset (Fin bottomCount), top : Finset (Fin middleCount); strictly layered OR-AND-OR
definitions_unfolded.gateCount: bottomCount + middleCount + 1 (all gates incl. output; matches S_3 total count)
definitions_unfolded.Computes: forall x, C.eval x = f x (exact)
definitions_unfolded.FiniteMultiTapeMachine: finite tape set K, finite alphabet with blank, finite states, partial transition code, accept : Q -> Bool; built on Mathlib Turing.Tape
definitions_unfolded.MultiTapeHaltsIn M w out time: exists k <= time and config c reached in k steps from init w with step c = none and accept c.q = out

D.label: D3
D.max_item: I07 Lemma restriction (cluster I11 expansion + I12 marker mixture + I15 backward averaging counting)

evidence.quote: Counting the resulting paths backwards cancels the number of eligible clauses against a reciprocal violation count. This is the source of the clause-count independence.

caveats: Switching-lemma family (Hastad, Razborov, SBI, Rossman, Lovett-Wu-Zhang) is a dense neighbourhood; an expert may know a CNF-to-CNF L1 expansion for constant pk.
If the restriction lemma is new, the remainder (sparsification, k-wise independence, PSZ00 slices, top-down counting) is N0-N2, so D3 rests on a single cluster.
Correctness assumed; the claim is extraordinary (see correctness_audit), though Lean-formalized end to end.

items.name: OR-AND-OR circuit and total gate count S_3(f)
items.statement: Depth-3 OR-AND-OR circuit, unbounded fan-in/fan-out, free input negations and constants, strictly layered; S_3(f) = minimum TOTAL number of AND and OR gates (bottom gates and output counted).

cited_or_new.cue: standard model; total-gate emphasis is the paper's

items.analytic_check: Analytic: occurs verbatim in the goal.

provisional_N.justification: Textbook depth-3 circuit model; total-gate count is the standard size measure.

items.name: sign g of a predicate; correlation |E gH| with a CNF indicator H
items.statement: g = +1 on accepted inputs, -1 otherwise; correlation of g with H is |E_x g(x)H(x)| under uniform x.

load_bearing_guess.reason: Every estimate is phrased in this quantity.

items.analytic_check: Analytic: standard Boolean-function-analysis vocabulary in L (correlation bounds literature).

items.name: clause, CNF, scope, width, normalized clause
items.statement: Clause = OR of literals; CNF = AND of clauses; after removing tautologies a nonconstant clause has distinct variables; scope = its variable set, width = |scope|; violated on exactly one assignment to its scope; false clause has empty scope.

items.name: C_b(V) and corr_b(G) = max over width-<=b CNF indicators J of |E GJ|
items.statement: C_b(V) = CNF indicators on {0,1}^V with clause widths <= b (no bound on clause count); corr_b(G) = max_{J in C_b(V)} |E_z G(z)J(z)|.

cited_or_new.cue: none; implicitly standard (correlation with a class)

load_bearing_guess.reason: The interface quantity between the restriction lemma and the hard-slice proposition.

items.analytic_check: Analytic: "max correlation with class C" is a standard pattern in L (correlation bounds vs AC0 / k-CNF); special case with C = width-b CNFs.

provisional_N.justification: Abbreviation: correlation with a fixed function class.

items.name: p-random restriction (T, rho), restricted function G_{T,rho}, and the averaging identity E_x GH = E_{T,rho} E_z G_{T,rho}H_{T,rho}
items.statement: T keeps each coordinate independently w.p. p; rho uniform outside T; filling T uniformly gives a uniform point, eq. (restriction-expectation).

items.name: cylinder (subcube) on the live set
items.statement: Prescribe a pattern on U subset T; indicator is a conjunction of unit clauses; measure 2^{-|U|}.

load_bearing_guess.reason: Used for J_P and the reweighting step.

items.name: Lemma restriction (Restriction bound): clause-count-independent signed CNF expansion under p-restriction
items.statement: For H a width-<=k CNF on [d], 0<p<1, b>=1, theta = sum_{l=b+1}^k C(k,l)(2p/(1-p))^l < 1: there are W(H,T,rho) >= 0 with E W <= 1/(1-theta) and |E_z G(z)H_{T,rho}(z)| <= W corr_b(G) simultaneously for all real G on {0,1}^T. No dependence on the number of clauses.

cited_or_new.cue: "This is a different conclusion from the classical switching estimate ... Here the tests remain CNFs" (02:9-12); intro: "Our main ingredient" (00:116)

load_bearing_guess.reason: Sole route from width k = Theta(sqrt d) to constant width b; without it the method is Hastad-limited to pk < const and gives only 2^{O(sqrt n)}. Lean closure 346/2046 decls (16.9% of whole DAG; ~38% of the 906-decl lower-bound half).

items.analytic_check: Non-analytic: neither the goal (a depth-3 size bound) nor L states a signed-CNF L1-mass expansion of restricted CNFs; nearest L statement is Hastad's switching lemma (H89 Main Lemma), which has a different conclusion (DNF/decision tree) and requires pk < const.

provisional_N.justification: Candidate. Quick lit check (Oct 2026): no statement found that expands a restricted width-k CNF into width-b CNF tests with expected coefficient mass <= 1/(1-theta) for ARBITRARY constant pk (b depending on pk). Neighbours: Hastad switching lemma (pk<1/5, DT depth), Razborov encoding proof, Segerlind-Buss-Impagliazzo small-restriction switching, Lovett-Wu-Zhang mild restrictions (first moment of useful terms), Gopalan-Meka-Reingold DNF sparsification. None gives this conclusion.

items.provisional_F: F3 (auxiliary construction: the path expansion + marker mixtures is a device built only to drive the proof), with F5 flavour (change of representation of H_{T,rho} as a signed mixture of CNFs)

items.name: easy/hard at U; counts a_U (violated easy clauses) and c_U (violated fully-revealed clauses); q
items.statement: Index i easy at U iff |E_i cap (T minus U)| <= b; a_U = sum of v_i over easy i; c_U = sum over i with E_i cap (T minus U) empty; q = total violated count.
items.analytic_check: Non-analytic relative to goal; resembles the "first surviving clause" bookkeeping of switching-lemma proofs.

provisional_N.justification: Part of I07; counting-of-violated-clauses normalisations have neighbours (PPZ isolation counting; Razborov encodings), but this specific easy/hard split is internal to I07.

items.name: K = conjunction of initially easy clauses after rho (width <= b CNF)
items.statement: K = 1[a_empty = 0]; K >= H_{T,rho}; first-order approximation of H.
items.analytic_check: Analytic-ish: truncation of a CNF to its narrow clauses is a common move (cf. I30).

items.name: violation paths P_j(T): sequences of successively hard clause indices with revealed sets U_h
items.statement: P = (i_1..i_j) with i_h hard at U_{h-1}, U_h = U_{h-1} cup (E_{i_h} cap T); each step reveals > b coords, so length <= |T|/(b+1); indices distinct; a_{U_h} >= c_{U_h} >= h on support.

load_bearing_guess.reason: Index set of the expansion and of W.

items.analytic_check: Non-analytic vs goal. Close in shape to the canonical decision tree / "successive first unsatisfied clause" paths in switching-lemma proofs (H89, Razborov).

provisional_N.justification: Variant of canonical-decision-tree paths, but selection is "any hard violated clause" (all of them, summed), not the first one.

items.name: Telescoping partition-of-unity expansion: 1 = sum_i v_i/q, r_P = t_P - sum_i r_{Pi}, giving H_{T,rho} = K + K sum_j (-1)^j sum_{P in P_j} prod v / prod a_{U_h} (pointwise, finite)
items.statement: Distribute the unit excess K - H among violated hard clauses with weights v_i/q, replace q by the count a_{U_j} of easy violated clauses, and push the remainder to longer paths; finite alternating expansion.

cited_or_new.cue: "The next step replaces the common denominator q by counts of easy clauses" (02:70)

items.analytic_check: Non-analytic: no subterm of goal or L. Generic neighbours: inclusion-exclusion / cluster (polymer) expansions; partitions of unity over violated constraints (e.g. Moser-Tardos-style witness trees use similar path bookkeeping).

provisional_N.justification: Part of the I07 cluster; no neighbour found that writes a CNF as an alternating sum over violation paths with violated-count denominators.

items.name: Marker mixture: random order of a clauses and c markers; conjunction of clauses before first marker has expectation c/(c+w)
items.statement: Represents the rational weight c/(c+w) (w = # violated clauses in an indexed family) as a convex mixture of conjunctions of those clauses, so every term K prod v / prod a equals omega(P) E[J_P] with J_P in C_b(T).

cited_or_new.cue: "We use the following elementary finite mixture" (02:168)

load_bearing_guess.reason: Keeps the tests inside C_b, which is what lets the bound be in terms of corr_b. Lean closure of pathMixture_scaled_average: 156 decls (7.6%).

items.analytic_check: Non-analytic vs goal; the probability that the first of w+c random objects is a marker is a classical symmetry fact (random-order / "first arrival" arguments).

provisional_N.justification: Elementary random-ordering identity (classical), used here in a new role: realizing reciprocal-count weights as convex combinations of CNFs. The use is new, the identity is N0.

items.name: path weight omega(P) = prod 1/c_h; W_j, W(H,T,rho) = sum over compatible paths
items.statement: Compatible paths (all selected clauses simultaneously violable with rho) prescribe a pattern sigma_P on U_j; c_{U_h} is constant on the cylinder; omega(P) = prod 1/c_h; W = sum_j W_j.

items.name: Reweighting by a full assignment y (E W_j = E_{T,y}[sum over paths violated at y of 2^{|U_j|} prod 1/c_{U_h}(y)])
items.statement: Sample y uniform, set rho = y outside T; conditional on (T,rho) multiply by 2^{|U_j|} to undo the cylinder probability.
items.analytic_check: Analytic: standard "sample the full assignment first" trick (Razborov / Beame proofs of the switching lemma).

items.name: Backward (reverse) path counting: injective reverse encoding from terminal set R_j, recursion F_s(R) = (1/|V_R|) sum_{i in V_R} sum_{D subset E_i,|D|>b} alpha^{|D|} F_{s-1}(R cup D) <= theta^s; the reciprocal count 1/|V_R| AVERAGES over clause indices, cancelling clause count
items.statement: With alpha = 2p/(1-p), pi(T) 2^{|U_j|} prod 1/c = pi(R_j) prod alpha^{|D_h|}/|V_{R_h}|; one-step weight <= theta; hence E W_j <= theta^j and E W <= 1/(1-theta).

cited_or_new.cue: "Counting the resulting paths backwards cancels the number of eligible clauses against a reciprocal violation count. This is the source of the clause-count independence." (00:126-128)

load_bearing_guess.reason: The quantitative heart of I07. Lean: weighted_supported_paths_le closure 79 decls; ReversePath* 64 decls, 648 lines.

items.analytic_check: Non-analytic. Shape-neighbour: Razborov's injective encoding of bad restrictions (aux info d log w), Rossman entropy proof; here the encoding runs backward from the terminal live set and the per-step factor is an average (1/|V_R| sum), not a log w bit cost.

provisional_N.justification: Part of I07 cluster; the averaging-instead-of-multiplying device is what removes the clause count and permits arbitrary constant pk.

items.name: theta = sum_{l=b+1}^k C(k,l)(2p/(1-p))^l
items.statement: Poisson-like tail; <= sum_{l>b} Q^l/l! with Q = 2pk/(1-p).

items.name: Lemma sparse-partition: every width-b CNF on m vars is a DISJOINT sum of <= 2^{eta m} width-b CNFs with <= M(b,eta) m clauses each
items.statement: For every b>=1, eta>0 there is M(b,eta) such that H = sum_{a<=q} H_a pointwise, q <= 2^{eta m}, H_a width <= b with <= Mm clauses, satisfying sets pairwise disjoint.

cited_or_new.cue: "The proof adapts the sparsification method of Impagliazzo, Paturi, and Zane ... A disjoint refinement is described by Dell, Husfeldt, Marx, Taslaman, and Wahlen ... Here we prove a version with the bookkeeping needed" (03:5-10)

load_bearing_guess.reason: Needed so a union bound over 2^{O(m log m)} sparse tests controls all width-b CNFs. Lean closure 196 decls (9.6%); Sparse* defs have frac_dag_dependents ~0.21-0.23.

items.analytic_check: Analytic vs L: the sparsification lemma (IPZ01) and its disjoint/counting version (DHMTW14, Calabro-Impagliazzo-Paturi 2006) are in L.

provisional_N.justification: Re-proof of the disjoint sparsification lemma (known, cited); restated with clause count Mm instead of variable-occurrence bounds.

items.name: sunflower, core, petals
items.statement: Distinct sets with common pairwise intersection C (core); petals = sets minus C.

items.name: Lemma sunflower-bound (Erdos-Rado): > s!(r-1)^s distinct s-sets contain an r-sunflower
items.statement: Classical, with proof by induction on s.

cited_or_new.cue: "We use the classical sunflower bound of Erdos and Rado ... and include its short proof" (03:27-28)

items.name: eligible sunflower at size i (r_i members, nonempty core); branching state = active antichain + separate unit-clause side condition; branch 0 inserts core C, branch 1 inserts petals and adds "C false" side condition
items.statement: F = F_0 + 1[C false] F_1 with disjoint supports.

cited_or_new.cue: "The extra requirement on branch 1 is the disjointness device of [DHMTW14, App. A]" (03:94-95)

items.analytic_check: Analytic vs L (IPZ01 branching, DHMTW14 disjointness).

provisional_N.justification: IPZ branching with DHMTW side condition; keeping the side condition separate from the active family is a bookkeeping refinement.

items.name: occurrence bounds e_i, added-clause invariant (<= e_u + 1 per literal), insertion charging N_u <= (e_u+1)(2m + sum_{v<u} N_v), budgets D_i
items.statement: Bounds the number of steps per path linearly in m.

items.name: leaf counting via per-size decision streams with few ones + binary entropy bound; threshold choice r_i = 2^{q_i}
items.statement: #leaves <= prod 2^{m F_i h_2(1/r_i)} <= 2^{eta m}.

provisional_N.justification: Standard entropy counting as in IPZ01.

items.name: Definition language: data x (d bits), Hankel/Toeplitz hash seed u, monic modulus P of degree r = ceil(d^{2/3}), t ~ d^{1/6} coefficients beta_j in F_2[Z]/(P); accept iff lambda(sum_j beta_j h(x)^j) = 0
items.statement: d = floor(n/5); r = ceil(d^{2/3}); t = largest even j with j^6 <= d; parameter bits are part of the input; evaluator never tests irreducibility.

cited_or_new.cue: "The input-index construction in [PSZ00, Section 5] supplies an earlier instance of this evaluator-and-hard-subfunction method" (04:10-11)

items.analytic_check: Non-analytic in the trivial sense (the goal is existential in L); the design is a standard pattern: k-wise independent function = polynomial of degree < t over GF(2^r) evaluated at a hash, with seed/coefficients as input bits (PSZ00 style).

provisional_N.justification: Close variant of PSZ00 input-index construction + ABI86/IPZ01 polynomial families; parameters r, t tuned to the sqrt(d) live sets.

items.name: Hankel (Toeplitz) linear hash h_i(x) = sum_s u_{i+s-1} x_s
items.statement: Universal linear hash; only uniformity of h(w) for nonzero w is used.

cited_or_new.cue: "Fully random Toeplitz matrices give a standard universal linear hash family" (04:51-52)

items.name: Prop polytime: L decided by one deterministic TM in time C(n+1)^a
items.statement: Integer parameter search, O(rd + t r^2) bit operations; no irreducibility test.

items.name: Prop good-slices: for fixed b, B and large n there is a setting of non-data bits whose slice g satisfies Pr_{T,rho}[|T| not in [m0/2, 2m0] or corr_b(g_{T,rho}) > 2^{-|T|/8}] <= 4 2^{-m0/16}, p = B/sqrt d, m0 = B sqrt d
items.statement: Probabilistic method over (u, beta): hash injective on the restricted cube w.p. >= 1 - 2^{m-r}; then signs t-wise independent; t-th moment + union over (C_m+1)^{Mm} sparse tests + sparse partition gives corr_b <= 2^{-m/8}; average over parameter choices.

cited_or_new.cue: "Sparse normal forms and random polynomial families also occur in [IPZ01, Section 1.2]" (00:154-155)

load_bearing_guess.reason: Supplies the b-independent correlation exponent 1/8 on random restrictions. Lean closure of exists_good_language_slice_eventually: 552 decls (27%).

items.analytic_check: Partly analytic: "random degree-2 polynomials / limited-independence functions have small correlation with sparse k-CNFs, via sparsification + union bound" is IPZ01 Sec 1.2 (in L). New: applying it on every random restriction with live-set size ~ B sqrt d and an exponent independent of b.

provisional_N.justification: Close variant of IPZ01's random-polynomial depth-3 (bounded bottom fan-in) argument, transplanted to restricted cubes.

items.name: h(w) uniform for every nonzero w (successive pivots), hence injectivity on a restricted m-cube except w.p. <= 2^{m-r}
items.statement: Union bound over 2^m - 1 differences.

items.name: limited independence from Lagrange interpolation: uniform beta in F^t gives t-wise independent unbiased signs on distinct hash values
items.statement: Evaluation map surjective for q <= t distinct nodes; lambda balanced.

items.name: count of sparse tests <= 2^{Mm[1 + b log2(2m+1)]}
items.statement: Encoding of normalized clauses and lists of <= Mm clauses.

items.name: t-th moment bound E Y^t <= t^t 2^{mt/2}, Markov, union bound
items.statement: Terms with a singleton point vanish; at most 2^{mt/2}(t/2)^t surviving descriptions.

provisional_N.justification: Standard moment method for k-wise independent sums.

items.name: binomial tails of |T| and averaging to fix one parameter setting
items.statement: Pr[m<m0/2], Pr[m>2m0] <= 2^{-m0/16} each; averaging argument.

items.name: Order of quantifiers and parameters: fix A, s = 3A, B = 64(s+1), p = B/sqrt d, k = ceil(3(s+1) sqrt d), Q = 4B[3(s+1)+1], then choose b = b(A) with sum_{l>b} Q^l/l! <= 1/2 so theta <= 1/2
items.statement: pk is a (large) constant depending on A; b is chosen after A so the restriction lemma applies; the slice is chosen after (b, B). "This is the only place where the desired circuit exponent affects the target width."

load_bearing_guess.reason: This is where the omega(sqrt n) comes from: arbitrary constant pk is allowed because b may grow with A while the slice's correlation exponent (1/8) does not depend on b.

proof_architecture.claim: Define the language: data block, Hankel hash seed, monic modulus, t coefficients; accept iff lambda(sum beta_j h(x)^j) = 0. It runs in polynomial time and never searches.
external: PSZ00 (idea of parameter bits as input)

proof_architecture.claim: Sparse partition: each width-b CNF on m vars is a disjoint sum of <= 2^{eta m} width-b CNFs with <= Mm clauses.

Good slices: for fixed (b, B) a parameter setting exists such that on most p-restrictions (p = B/sqrt d) the restricted slice has corr_b <= 2^{-|T|/8}, via hash injectivity, t-wise independence, t-th moment, union bound over sparse tests.

Restriction lemma: any width-k CNF restricted by (T, rho) correlates with G at most W corr_b(G), E W <= 1/(1-theta), clause-count independent; built from the path expansion, marker mixtures and backward averaging count.
Parameters: fix A, then B, k = Theta(sqrt d), Q = O(pk), b = b(A) with Poisson tail <= 1/2; transfer correlation to all width-k CNFs: |E gH| <= 6 2^{-m0/16}.
Circuit counting: truncate middle CNFs at width k, each accepts <= 6 2^{-m0/16} + S 2^{-k}; S <= 2^{A sqrt n} contradicts acceptance density >= 1/4.

eureka_candidates.item: I07 Lemma restriction, as the cluster I11 (telescoping violation-path expansion) + I12 (marker mixture keeping tests in C_b) + I15 (backward averaging count: 1/|V_R| averages over clause indices)
for: It is the step that breaks the sqrt n barrier: it allows any constant pk (b chosen after A), while every switching-lemma statement in L needs pk below an absolute constant.
Conclusion type (signed CNF mixture with L1 cost, clause-count free, tests stay CNFs) is not a subterm of the goal or of L; the paper itself contrasts it with Hastad.
Load-bearing: 346/2046 Lean decls (16.9% of whole DAG, ~38% of the lower-bound half); nothing else lifts width.
Pieces are tiny identities (1 = sum v_i/q; c/(c+w) as marker mixture) that do not appear in the goal, in the Cook-PHP sense.
against: Dense neighbourhood: Razborov encoding proofs, SBI small-restriction switching lemma, Lovett-Wu-Zhang mild-restriction lemma (bounds first moment of useful terms for width-w DNFs at any constant restriction rate), Rossman entropy proof, GMR DNF sparsification. An expert may recognise I07 as a variant.
Backward encoding with reweighting by a full assignment is a known technique family.
The lemma alone is not the lower bound; it needs the b-independent pseudorandom slice (I26).
eureka_candidates.nearest_neighbour: Lovett, Wu, Zhang, "Decision list compression by mild random restrictions" (STOC 2020, arXiv 1909.10658): under a mild restriction, width-w DNFs have 2^{O(w)} useful terms in expectation (first moment). Also Hastad H89 Main Lemma; Segerlind-Buss-Impagliazzo 2004.

correctness_audit.verdict: No gap found on a line-by-line reading of sections 2-5. The claim is extraordinary: it resolves the 2^{omega(sqrt n)} explicit depth-3 lower bound question that the cited literature (GPPST24, GKPRT26) and a community problem list (verified 2026-08-10) treat as open. The Lean development proves the comparator statement end to end with no sorry/axiom, which (if it builds) removes most correctness risk, leaving only definitional faithfulness, which checks out.
checked: Restriction lemma, expansion identity: verified the cases K=0, q=0, and K=1/q>0; residual identity r_P = t_P - sum r_{Pi} uses q = a_{U_j} + sum_{hard} v_i (02:105-112).
Restriction lemma, marker mixture: K prod v/prod a = omega(P) E[J_P] on and off the cylinder; J_P has width <= b (needs b >= 1 for unit clauses).
Restriction lemma, expected cost: reverse encoding injective; pi(T)2^{|U_j|} = pi(R_j) alpha^{|U_j|}; one-step weight <= theta by monotonicity in |E_i| <= k (02:309-316).
Sanity examples worked by hand: single width-k clause (E W = 1 + Pr[unsatisfied by rho and > b live]) and parity-as-CNF (W = 1 + 2^{l-1}, paid by alpha^l); both consistent with E W <= 1 + theta-ish.
Good slices: union-bound condition M[1+b log(2m+1)]/t + log t/m <= 1/8 holds since t ~ d^{1/6} >> log d and m ~ sqrt d (04:239-246); hash failure 2^{m-r} with r ~ d^{2/3} >> m.
Final arithmetic: m0/16 = 4(s+1) sqrt d > s sqrt d + O(1); k >= 3(s+1) sqrt d > 2 s sqrt d; Q constant so b = b(A) exists (05:26-44, 127-136).
Why parity is not a counterexample to the method: corr_b(parity_m) ~ 2^{-Theta(m/b)}, so the bound degrades as b grows with A; consistent with PPZ99 tightness.
Comparator definitions faithful (gate count includes bottom + middle + output; exact computation; machine time bound C(n+1)^a).
residual_concerns: Lean not compiled here; the end-to-end guarantee is conditional on the release CI build.

Rate is ineffective: b(A) and M(b, 1/8) grow extremely fast (M is tower-like in b via e_i = (i-1)!(r_i-1)^{i-1} with r_i chosen after F_i), so the omega in 2^{omega(sqrt n)} is astronomically slow; the paper does not claim any rate.

The hard slice is chosen by the probabilistic method; the language is explicit (in P) only because the parameter bits are inputs (PSZ00-style). This is a standard but weaker notion of explicitness than a fixed natural function like Majority.
The function depends on only r = d^{2/3} linear forms of the data (g = G(Mx)); the proof never needs more, but this is worth noting for anyone looking for a structural attack.
No independent expert verification; the result is unreviewed.
